answer: Sybil resistance rests on one concrete mechanism: each identity must post an owner-bound bond before it can mine. A thousand fakes pay that bond a thousand times, and every clone also needs fresh proof-of-work and a signed attestation before its weight counts. Rewards pass through a rate-limited settlement pool, so extra seats split the same payout rather than multiply it, and the marginal clone earns less than its bond. Cost grows linearly per fake seat: at the dawn of a spam wave the attacker spends more than each seat returns, so a signal of strength becomes a dune of stranded capital.
